question: Your team uses Claude Code to generate a new payment validation module. A developer then asks the generation session, which is the Claude Code session that wrote the code, to review the changes before merging. The review reports no problems, but a teammate later finds several logic errors in the module. Which change would most effectively improve the quality of this review?

options.text: Ask the generation session to report its findings with --output-format json and --json-schema so that the results are machine-parseable.
options.reason: These flags only make the output structured; the review still runs in the generation session, so it stays less effective than an independent review instance.

options.text: Resume the generation session with --resume so that the review keeps full knowledge of the original design decisions.
options.reason: Resuming the generation session carries over its context, and the guide says that a review in the generation session is less effective than an independent review instance.

options.text: Add an instruction in the generation session that tells Claude to review its own changes more critically before approving them.
options.reason: The review still runs in the generation session, so the session context isolation problem that the guide describes remains.

options.text: Run the review in an independent review instance of Claude Code that starts without the context of the generation session.
options.reason: The guide states that an independent review instance reviews changes more effectively than the generation session, which keeps the context in which it produced the code.
